words.ex: He bought a single ticket to the concert.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一张音乐会的单程票。
words.en: A ticket for a journey to a place but not back again.

words.ex: He bought a one-way ticket to New York.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一张去纽约的单程票。
words.en: A ticket for travel from one place to another but not back again.

words.ex: He bought a return ticket to London.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一张去伦敦的往返票。
words.en: A return ticket is a ticket for a journey to a place and back again.

words.ex: He bought a round-trip ticket to Paris.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一张去巴黎的往返票。
words.en: A ticket that allows you to travel to a place and then return back to where you started.

words.ex: I bought a day return ticket to the city.
words.ex_cn: 我买了一张往返市里的票。

words.tr: phrase. 季票；（在一定期限内可多次使用的）通票
words.ex: He buys a season ticket for the football matches.
words.ex_cn: 他购买了足球比赛的季票。
words.en: A season ticket is a ticket that allows the holder to attend a specified number of events, such as sports games or concerts, within a certain period, usually a season, for a single price.

words.tr: phrase. 周票和月票（指按周或按月计费的交通票券）
words.ex: He buys a weekly monthly ticket for the subway.
words.ex_cn: 他购买地铁的周票和月票。

words.tr: phrase. 非高峰时段票；非高峰期车票
words.ex: I bought an off-peak ticket to save money.
words.ex_cn: 我买了一张非高峰时段票来省钱。

words.tr: phrase. 任意时间票（可随时使用的票，通常用于交通或活动）
words.ex: I bought an anytime ticket so I can take the train whenever I want.
words.ex_cn: 我买了一张任意时间票，这样我就可以随时坐火车。

words.tr: phrase. 提前购买的票；预售票
words.ex: He bought an advance ticket for the concert.
words.ex_cn: 他提前买了音乐会的票。
words.en: A ticket purchased in advance of travel, often at a discounted rate.

words.ex: The adult ticket costs ten dollars.
words.ex_cn: 成人票十美元。
words.en: A ticket priced for general adult passengers, typically higher than discounted fares.

words.ex: He bought a child ticket for the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他为这部电影买了一张儿童票。

words.ex: He bought a student ticket for the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一张学生票来看电影。
words.en: A discounted ticket available to students upon presenting valid identification.

words.tr: phrase. 老年人票；老年优惠票
words.ex: He bought a senior ticket for the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他买了张老年人票来看电影。

words.tr: phrase. 优惠票；特惠票（指学生、老人等享受折扣的票）
words.ex: He bought a concession ticket for the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他买了电影的优惠票。

words.ex: We bought a family ticket for the zoo.
words.ex_cn: 我们买了一张家庭票去动物园。
words.en: A family ticket is a type of admission ticket that allows a group of people, typically consisting of two adults and a certain number of children, to enter an event or venue at a reduced rate compared to purchasing individual tickets.

words.tr:
n. 车费；费用；
v. 进展；成功（或不成功等）；
words.ex: The bus fare is two dollars.
words.ex_cn: 公交车费是两美元。
words.en: The fare is the amount of money that you pay for a journey that you make, for example, in a bus, train, or taxi.

words.ex: Children under 12 can travel at half price, but adults must pay the full fare.
words.ex_cn: 12岁以下的儿童可以半价旅行，但成人必须支付全价票。
words.en: The complete price for a ticket without any discounts.

words.ex: He bought a discount fare for the train trip.
words.ex_cn: 他买了火车旅行的折扣票价。

words.ex: You need to pay a booking fee to reserve the hotel room.
words.ex_cn: 你需要支付预订费来预订酒店房间。
words.en: a charge for making a reservation

words.tr: phrase. 信用卡附加费；对使用信用卡支付额外收取的费用
words.ex: The store added a credit card surcharge for payments.
words.ex_cn: 商店对信用卡付款加收了附加费。

words.ex: You need to pay a 40-yuan deposit to rent the bike.
words.ex_cn: 租自行车需要支付40元押金。
words.en: A deposit is a sum of money which is part of the full price of something, and which you pay when you agree to buy it. It is also a sum of money that you pay into a bank account.

words.tr:
n. 平衡；天平；秤；
v. （使）相抵；（使）平衡；
words.ex: She maintains a good balance between work and rest.
words.ex_cn: 她在工作和休息之间保持良好的平衡。
words.en: Balance is the ability to remain steady when you are standing up. Also, it refers to the state of having your weight spread equally so that you do not fall. In finance, it refers to the amount of money you have in a bank account.

words.ex: He bought a train ticket at the ticket office.
words.ex_cn: 他在售票处买了一张火车票。
words.en: A ticket office is a place where tickets are sold to the public for admission to a theater, for travel on public transportation, etc.

words.tr: phrase. 售票处；预订办公室
words.ex: He went to the booking office to buy a train ticket.
words.ex_cn: 他去售票处买了一张火车票。
words.en: An office where reservations for travel, events, or accommodations are made and confirmed.

words.tr: phrase. 售票机；自动售票机
words.ex: He bought a ticket from the ticket machine.
words.ex_cn: 他从自动售票机买了一张票。
words.en: A ticket machine is a machine from which you can buy tickets, for example for travel on public transport or for entry to a cinema or theatre.

words.ex: I bought a train ticket from the ticket vending machine.
words.ex_cn: 我从自动售票机买了火车票。

words.ex: He asked for help at the information desk.
words.ex_cn: 他在信息台寻求帮助。
words.en: A place in a public building where you can go to get information.

words.ex: He booked his flight through a travel agency.
words.ex_cn: 他通过一家旅行社预订了航班。
words.en: A travel agency is a business that helps people plan and book trips and vacations.

words.ex: I bought books from an online website.
words.ex_cn: 我从一个网站买了书。

words.ex: He uses an app to learn English.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个应用程序来学习英语。
words.en: An app is a computer program that is designed for a specific purpose, especially one that can be downloaded onto a mobile device.

words.tr:
n. 书；账簿；
v. 预订；
words.ex: I read a book before sleep.
words.ex_cn: 我睡觉前读了一本书。
words.en: A book is a number of pieces of paper, usually with words printed on them, which are fastened together and fixed inside a cover of stronger paper or cardboard. Books contain information, stories, or poetry, for example.

words.tr:
n. 保护区；储备；保留；
v. 预订；
words.ex: The wildlife reserve is home to many endangered animals.
words.ex_cn: 这个自然保护区是许多濒危动物的家园。
words.en: If you reserve something such as a table, ticket, or magazine, you arrange for it to be kept for you and not given to anyone else.

words.ex: I will make a reservation for two people.
words.ex_cn: 我将为两个人预订。
words.en: To book or arrange for something in advance, such as a table at a restaurant.

words.tr:
n. 购买；采购；
v. 购买；采购；
words.ex: The purchase of a new car took all his savings.
words.ex_cn: 买一辆新车花光了他所有的积蓄。
words.en: To purchase something means to buy it. It can also refer to something that has been bought.

words.ex: I buy apples at the market.
words.ex_cn: 我在市场买苹果。
words.en: To buy means to obtain something by paying money for it.

words.ex: He will cancel the meeting tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会取消会议。
words.en: If you cancel something that has been arranged, you stop it from happening. If you cancel an order for goods or services, you tell the person or organization supplying them that you no longer wish to receive them.

words.ex: I asked for a refund after the product broke.
words.ex_cn: 产品坏了之后，我要求退款。
words.en: A refund is a sum of money that is returned to you, for example because you have paid too much or because you have returned goods to a shop.

words.ex: Please give me your booking reference to check your flight.
words.ex_cn: 请给我你的电子客票订单号，以便查询你的航班。
words.en: A unique code or number provided to confirm a reservation for a flight, hotel, or other service.

words.ex: I received a confirmation email after booking the flight.
words.ex_cn: 我预订航班后收到了一封确认邮件。
words.en: An automated electronic message sent to confirm receipt of a request, transaction, or registration.

words.ex: He bought an e-ticket for the flight.
words.ex_cn: 他为航班购买了一张电子票。
words.en: An e-ticket is a digital ticket used for events, travel, or other activities, which can be stored on a mobile device or printed out.

words.ex: He still prefers to use paper tickets for train travel.
words.ex_cn: 他仍然更喜欢使用纸质车票乘坐火车。
words.en: A physical ticket made of paper, as opposed to an electronic or digital version.

words.tr: phrase. 火车优惠卡；铁路乘车卡（用于购买折扣火车票的证件）
words.ex: He uses a rail card to save money on train tickets.
words.ex_cn: 他使用铁路卡节省火车票费用。
words.en: A rail card is a card that allows the holder to get discounts on train tickets.

words.ex: I wait for the bus at station 15.
words.ex_cn: 我在15号车站等公交车。
words.en: A station is a place where trains, buses, or other vehicles regularly stop so that people can get on or off, or where a particular activity or service is based.

words.tr: phrase. 公交车站；公共汽车站
words.ex: He waits for the bus at the bus station.
words.ex_cn: 他在公交站等车。
words.en: A bus station is a place where buses start and end their routes, and where passengers can get on and off buses.

words.tr: phrase. 汽车站；长途汽车站（专供长途客车停靠和乘客上下车的场所）
words.ex: The bus stops at the coach station near the city center.
words.ex_cn: 公共汽车在市中心附近的长途汽车站停靠。
words.en: A coach station is a place where long-distance buses start and finish their journeys, and where passengers can get on and off.

words.ex: The bus stops at the terminal at 9 PM.
words.ex_cn: 公交车晚上9点到达终点站。
words.en: A terminal is a place where vehicles, passengers, or goods begin or end a journey. It can also refer to a computer device at which a user enters data or commands.

words.ex: The teacher stood on the platform to speak.
words.ex_cn: 老师站在平台上讲话。
words.en: A platform is a flat, raised structure, usually made of wood, which people stand on when they make speeches or give performances.

words.ex: We sat in the waiting room for an hour.
words.ex_cn: 我们在候诊室坐了一个小时。
words.en: A room provided for the use of people who are waiting, as for an appointment or service.

words.ex: We waited in the lounge before our flight.
words.ex_cn: 我们在登机前等在休息室里。
words.en: A lounge is a room in a house or public building where people can sit and relax. As a verb, to lounge means to lie, sit, or stand in a relaxed or lazy way.

words.ex: He parked his car in the car park.
words.ex_cn: 他把车停在了停车场。
words.en: A car park is an area or building where people can leave their cars.

words.ex: The car is in the parking lot.
words.ex_cn: 车在停车场里。
words.en: A parking lot is an area of ground where people can leave their cars.

words.tr: phrase. 检票闸机；验票栏杆（用于车站、地铁等场所控制进出）
words.ex: He walked through the ticket barrier to enter the station.
words.ex_cn: 他通过检票闸机进入车站。
words.en: A ticket barrier is a gate or barrier at a railway station, subway station, or similar place that prevents people from passing through unless they insert a valid ticket.

words.ex: He closed the gate before it rained.
words.ex_cn: 下雨前他关上了门。
words.en: A gate is a structure like a door which is used at the entrance to a field, a garden, or the grounds of a building.

words.ex: He dropped his bag at the left luggage office.
words.ex_cn: 他把包寄存在行李寄存处。

words.tr: phrase. 行李寄存柜；行李储物柜
words.ex: He put his luggage in a locker at the station.
words.ex_cn: 他把行李放在了车站的储物柜里。
words.en: A luggage locker is a small compartment or storage space, typically found in public places like airports or train stations, where travelers can temporarily store their bags or belongings for a fee.

words.ex: He went to the lost property office to find his wallet.
words.ex_cn: 他去失物招领处找他的钱包。

words.ex: The toilet is broken and needs repair.
words.ex_cn: 马桶坏了，需要修理。
words.en: A toilet is a large bowl connected to the plumbing and used for urinating and defecating, typically fitted with a seat and flushing device.

words.tr: n. 厕所；洗手间；休息室；更衣室
words.ex: He went to the restroom after lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午饭后去了洗手间。
words.en: A restroom is a room in a public building with toilets and sinks for people to use.

words.ex: He drinks coffee at a small cafe.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家小咖啡馆喝咖啡。
words.en: A cafe is a small restaurant where drinks and snacks are sold.

words.tr: n. 售货亭；报刊亭；公用电话亭
words.ex: He bought a ticket from the kiosk.
words.ex_cn: 他从自动售票机买了一张票。
words.en: A kiosk is a small open-fronted hut or cubicle from which newspapers, refreshments, tickets, etc., are sold.

words.ex: I withdrew cash from the atm near the bank.
words.ex_cn: 我在银行附近的自动取款机取了现金。
words.en: An ATM is a machine that allows people to take out money from their bank accounts by using a special card. ATM can also refer to Asynchronous Transfer Mode, a telecommunications concept defined by ANSI and ITU (formerly CCITT) standards for carriage of a complete range of user traffic, including voice, data, and video signals.

words.tr: n. 时间表；时刻表；课程表；
words.ex: The school publishes a new timetable every term.
words.ex_cn: 学校每学期都会公布新的时间表。
words.en: A timetable is a detailed plan showing the times at which things are intended to happen, especially the times at which particular events or activities are planned to occur.

words.ex: I checked the class schedule for tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我查看了明天的课程时间表。
words.en: A schedule is a plan that gives a list of events or tasks and the times at which each one should happen or be done.

words.tr: phrase. 出发时间；离港时间
words.ex: The departure time is 8 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 出发时间是早上8点。
words.en: The scheduled time at which a vehicle, especially a train, bus, or aircraft, is supposed to leave a place.

words.tr: phrase. 到达时间；抵达时刻
words.ex: The arrival time of the train is 5 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 火车的到达时间是下午5点。
words.en: The time at which someone or something arrives at a place.

words.ex: The duration of the movie is two hours.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的持续时间是两小时。
words.en: The duration of an event or state is the time during which it happens or exists.

words.tr: phrase. 旅程时间；行程所需时间
words.ex: The journey time from Beijing to Shanghai is about five hours by train.
words.ex_cn: 从北京到上海的旅程时间大约是五个小时火车。

words.tr:
n. 推迟；延缓；耽搁；
v. 推迟；延缓；耽搁；
words.ex: The flight had a delay because of the storm.
words.ex_cn: 由于风暴，航班推迟了。
words.en: If you delay doing something, you do not do it immediately or at the planned or expected time, but you leave it until later.

words.tr: phrase. 落后于计划；误点；拖延的
words.ex: The train is behind schedule.
words.ex_cn: 火车晚点了。
words.en: If someone or something is behind schedule, they are not progressing as quickly as planned or expected.

words.tr: n. 取消；撤销；作废；中止；
words.ex: The flight cancellation made us wait for a new ticket.
words.ex_cn: 航班取消让我们不得不等待新的机票。
words.en: The act of cancelling something; a situation in which something that has been arranged is stopped from happening.

words.ex: Please complete the check-in at the front desk.
words.ex_cn: 请在前台完成签到。
words.en: The act of reporting one's presence, especially at a hotel or an airport, or the place where this happens.

words.tr: n. 寄膳（宿）； v. “board”的现在分词；
words.ex: The students pay for boarding at the school.
words.ex_cn: 学生们为学校的寄宿支付费用。
words.en: Boarding refers to the act of getting on or into a vehicle, ship, or aircraft, or the provision of meals and lodging for payment.

words.tr: phrase. 登机牌；用于登机时的身份凭证
words.ex: He showed his boarding pass at the gate.
words.ex_cn: 他在登机口出示了登机牌。
words.en: A boarding pass is a document provided by an airline during check-in, giving a passenger permission to board the airplane for a particular flight.

words.ex: They traveled by rail to visit their grandparents.
words.ex_cn: 他们乘火车去探望祖父母。
words.en: Using the railway system for transportation.

words.ex: I go to work by train every day.
words.ex_cn: 我每天坐火车去上班。
words.en: Using the train as a means of transportation.

words.tr: phrase. 乘长途汽车；坐长途客车
words.ex: They traveled by coach to the city.
words.ex_cn: 他们乘长途汽车去的城市。
words.en: Traveling by a long-distance bus.

words.ex: He goes to school by bus.
words.ex_cn: 他乘公交车去学校。
words.en: Using a bus as a means of transportation.

words.ex: We went to the island by ferry.
words.ex_cn: 我们乘渡轮去了那个岛。
words.en: Using a boat for transportation across water.

words.ex: He goes to work by tram.
words.ex_cn: 他乘有轨电车上班。

words.ex: He goes to work by light rail.
words.ex_cn: 他乘轻轨上班。

words.tr: phrase. 乘地铁；通过地下通道
words.ex: He goes to work by underground every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天乘地铁上班。
words.en: Using the subway system for transport.

words.ex: He travels to work by tube.
words.ex_cn: 他乘地铁去上班。
words.en: Via a subway or underground train system.

words.ex: I go to work by subway.
words.ex_cn: 我乘地铁去上班。
words.en: Using the subway as a means of transportation.

words.ex: He goes to work by metro every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天乘地铁上班。

words.tr:
n. 车费；费用；
v. 进展；成功（或不成功等）；
words.ex: The bus fare is two dollars.
words.ex_cn: 公交车费是两美元。
words.en: The fare is the amount of money that you pay for a journey that you make, for example, in a bus, train, or taxi.

words.ex: The teacher stood on the platform to speak.
words.ex_cn: 老师站在平台上讲话。
words.en: A platform is a flat, raised structure, usually made of wood, which people stand on when they make speeches or give performances.

words.ex: The king rode in a wooden carriage drawn by four horses.
words.ex_cn: 国王乘坐一辆由四匹马拉的木制四轮马车。
words.en: A carriage is a vehicle with four wheels that is pulled by horses and is used for carrying people.

words.ex: I take the bus to school every day.
words.ex_cn: 我每天乘公共汽车去学校。
words.en: A bus is a large motor vehicle which carries passengers from one place to another.

words.tr:
n. 教练；长途客运汽车；
v. 训练；培训；
words.ex: The coach taught the team how to win.
words.ex_cn: 教练教球队如何获胜。
words.en: A coach is someone who trains a person or team in a particular sport. It also refers to a large, comfortable bus that carries passengers on long journeys.

words.tr:
n. 火车；列车；列；队；
v. 训练；培训；
words.ex: I took the train to work this morning.
words.ex_cn: 今天早上我坐火车去上班。
words.en: A train is a number of carriages or trucks which are all connected together and which are pulled by an engine along a railway. Train also means to teach someone the skills of a particular job or activity, or to be taught these skills.

words.tr:
conj. 但是；然而；
prep. 除…以外；
adv. 只能；仅仅；
words.ex: I like apples, but I don't like oranges.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢苹果，但是我不喜欢橙子。
words.en: used to introduce a phrase or clause contrasting with what has already been mentioned

words.tr: adv. 事实上；实际上；竟然；
words.ex: I thought he was late, but actually he was on time.
words.ex_cn: 我以为他迟到了，但事实上他准时到了。
words.en: You use actually to indicate that a situation exists or happened, or to emphasize that it is true.

words.tr: adv. 然而；不过；不论到什么程度；无论如何；
words.ex: I like coffee; however, I drink tea in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢咖啡；然而，我早上喝茶。
words.en: You use however when you are adding a comment which is surprising or which contrasts with what has just been said.

words.tr: 短语动词. 购买一张票
words.ex: I need to buy a ticket for the concert tonight.
words.ex_cn: 我需要买今晚音乐会的票。
words.en: To purchase a ticket for an event or journey.

words.ex: He purchased a fare to Beijing yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天买了一张去北京的车票。

words.tr: phrase. 不可获得的；无法得到的；无现货的；不可用的
words.ex: The book is not available in the library.
words.ex_cn: 这本书在图书馆里没有。
words.en: If something is not available, it is not able to be used, obtained, or reached at a particular time.

words.ex: The concert tickets were sold out in one hour.
words.ex_cn: 音乐会门票在一个小时内就售罄了。
words.en: If a performance, sports event, or other entertainment is sold out, all the tickets for it have been sold.

words.ex: Please pay in advance.
words.ex_cn: 请提前付款。
words.en: Before a particular time, or before doing a particular thing.

words.tr: phrase. 提前进行；抢先行动
words.ex: We did ahead the project to finish early.
words.ex_cn: 我们提前完成了项目。

words.tr: adj. 单一的；单独的；单身的；
words.ex: He bought a single ticket for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一张单程公交车票。
words.en: Only one in number; one only; not married or not involved in a stable romantic relationship.

words.tr:
n. 返回；归还；
v. 返回；归还；
words.ex: The return of the train was delayed.
words.ex_cn: 火车的返回被推迟了。
words.en: To go or come back to a place or person. To give, send, or put something back to its original place or condition.

words.ex: Spring is a beautiful season.
words.ex_cn: 春天是一个美丽的季节。
words.en: A season is one of the four periods of the year: spring, summer, autumn, or winter. It can also refer to a period of the year characterized by particular conditions of weather, temperature, etc., or a period of the year when a particular sport is played.

words.ex: He uses a credit card to buy food.
words.ex_cn: 他用信用卡买食物。
words.en: A credit card is a small plastic card that you use to buy things on credit or to borrow money.

words.tr: phrase. 借记卡；签帐卡；提款卡
words.ex: I use my debit card to buy food.
words.ex_cn: 我用我的借记卡买食物。
words.en: A debit card is a plastic card which can be used to pay for things directly from your bank account when you are shopping, or to withdraw money from a cash machine.

words.ex: He paid with cash for the bread.
words.ex_cn: 他用现金买了面包。
words.en: Money in the form of coins or banknotes, especially that which is immediately available.

words.ex: We travel during off-peak hours to save money.
words.ex_cn: 我们在非高峰时段出行以节省费用。
words.en: Used to describe a time when something is less busy or less active, especially a time when fewer people are using a service or traveling.

words.ex: I bought a day return ticket to the city.
words.ex_cn: 我买了一张往返市里的票。

words.ex: The factory uses a big machine to make cars.
words.ex_cn: 工厂用一台大机器制造汽车。
words.en: A machine is a piece of equipment which uses electricity or an engine in order to do a particular kind of work.

words.tr: phrase. 信用卡附加费；刷卡手续费
words.ex: The store added a card surcharge for credit card payments.
words.ex_cn: 商店对信用卡支付加收了附加费。

words.tr:
n. 柜台；
v. 抵消；反驳；
adv. 相反地；
words.ex: The customer paid at the counter.
words.ex_cn: 顾客在柜台付款。
words.en: A counter is a long flat surface in a shop or bank on which customers are served. It can also refer to a device that counts something, or an action taken to oppose something.

words.tr:
n. 疼痛；隐痛；渴望
v. 疼痛；隐痛
words.ex: My head aches after staying up late.
words.ex_cn: 我熬夜后头痛。
words.en: If you ache or a part of your body aches, you feel a steady, fairly strong pain.

words.tr: n. 头痛；令人头痛的人（或事物）；
words.ex: He got a headache after working too long.
words.ex_cn: 他工作太长时间后得了头痛。
words.en: A headache is a pain in your head. If you say that something is a headache, you mean that it causes you difficulty or worry.

words.ex: He has a stomach ache after eating too much candy.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了太多糖果后肚子疼。
words.en: A pain in the stomach, often caused by eating too much or by an illness.

words.ex: He has a backache after lifting the box.
words.ex_cn: 他搬完箱子后背疼。
words.en: A backache is a pain in your back.

words.ex: He felt great pain after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他感到极大的痛苦。
words.en: Pain is the feeling of great discomfort you have, for example when you have been hurt or when you are ill.

words.ex: He felt a sharp pain in his leg.
words.ex_cn: 他感到腿里一阵剧痛。
words.en: A sharp pain is a sudden and intense feeling of discomfort or hurt.

words.ex: He felt a dull pain in his back after lifting the box.
words.ex_cn: 他搬完箱子后感到背部有一种钝痛。
words.en: A dull pain is a pain that is not sharp or intense, but rather a constant, mild ache or discomfort.

words.ex: He hurt his leg while playing soccer.
words.ex_cn: 他在踢足球时伤了腿。
words.en: If you hurt someone, you cause them to feel pain. If you hurt a part of your body, you feel pain there. If someone is hurt, they are injured.

words.ex: My throat is sore after singing.
words.ex_cn: 我唱歌后喉咙疼。
words.en: If part of your body is sore, it causes you pain and discomfort.

words.ex: He has a sore throat from singing too much.
words.ex_cn: 他因为唱太多歌而喉咙痛。
words.en: If you have a sore throat, your throat hurts and it is difficult for you to swallow.

words.ex: He had sore muscles after running five kilometers.
words.ex_cn: 他跑完五公里后肌肉酸痛。

words.ex: His neck was stiff after sleeping wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他睡姿不对，脖子变得僵硬。
words.en: If something is stiff, it is firm and does not bend easily. It can also describe a person who is not relaxed or friendly.

words.ex: He has a stiff neck from sleeping wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他因为睡姿不对导致脖子僵硬。
words.en: A condition where the neck muscles are tight and painful, making it difficult to move the head.

words.tr:
adj. 肿胀的；上涨的
v. 膨胀；肿胀；“swell”的过去分词
words.ex: His ankle is swollen after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 他摔倒后脚踝肿了。
words.en: If a part of your body is swollen, it is larger and rounder than normal, usually as a result of injury or illness.

words.ex: He has a swollen ankle from playing soccer.
words.ex_cn: 他踢足球后脚踝肿了。
words.en: An ankle that is enlarged due to fluid accumulation or injury.

words.tr:
v. 扭伤
n. 扭伤
words.ex: He sprained his ankle while running.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步时扭伤了脚踝。
words.en: If you sprain a joint such as your ankle or wrist, you accidentally damage it by twisting it or bending it violently.

words.ex: He has a sprained wrist from playing basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他打篮球时扭伤了手腕。

words.ex: He hurt his ankle and now has a sprained ankle.
words.ex_cn: 他扭伤了脚踝，现在脚踝扭伤了。
words.en: An injury to the ligaments around the ankle joint, typically caused by a sudden twist or turn that results in pain, swelling, and difficulty walking.

words.tr:
n. 压力；（动植物的）品种；
v. 竭力；
words.ex: The job gave him a lot of strain.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作给他带来了很大的压力。
words.en: To strain means to make a great effort to do something, to pull or stretch something tightly, or to injure a muscle by stretching it too much.

words.ex: He got a muscle strain after lifting heavy boxes.
words.ex_cn: 他搬重箱子后造成了肌肉拉伤。

words.ex: He fractured his arm during the soccer game.
words.ex_cn: 他在足球比赛中摔断了手臂。
words.en: If something such as a bone fractures or is fractured, it breaks or cracks.

words.tr: phrase. 发丝状骨折；细微骨折
words.ex: He has a hairline fracture in his wrist.
words.ex_cn: 他的手腕有一条细小的骨折。
words.en: A very fine crack in a bone that does not completely break it.

words.tr:
v. 切；割；削减；
n. 切；割；削减；
words.ex: He cut the apple with a knife.
words.ex_cn: 他用刀切了苹果。
words.en: To make an opening, incision, or wound in (something) with a sharp-edged tool or object.

words.tr: v. 擦伤；挫伤；出现伤痕；
words.ex: He bruised his knee when he fell off the bike.
words.ex_cn: 他从自行车上摔下来时擦伤了膝盖。
words.en: A bruise is a mark that appears on your skin after you have been injured, but the skin is not broken.

words.ex: The wood burns slowly in the fire.
words.ex_cn: 木头在火中缓慢燃烧。
words.en: If there is a fire or a flame somewhere, you say that there is a burn there. When you burn something, you destroy or damage it with fire or heat.

words.tr: n. 关节错位；脱臼；混乱
words.ex: The fall caused a dislocation in his shoulder.
words.ex_cn: 这次跌倒导致他的肩膀脱臼。
words.en: Dislocation refers to the displacement of something from its usual position or state, often used in the context of bones moving out of place in the body or the disruption of systems and structures.

words.ex: He fell off his bike and got a dislocated shoulder.
words.ex_cn: 他从自行车上摔下来，导致肩关节脱位。

words.tr: adj. 头晕目眩的；头昏眼花的；
words.ex: He felt dizzy after spinning around quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速转圈后感到头晕目眩。
words.en: If you feel dizzy, you feel that you are losing your balance and are about to fall.

words.ex: The smell of the food made her feel nausea.
words.ex_cn: 食物的气味让她感到恶心。
words.en: A feeling of sickness with an inclination to vomit.

words.ex: He has a high fever and stays in bed.
words.ex_cn: 他发烧了，躺在床上休息。
words.en: A fever is a condition in which the body's temperature is higher than usual, often as a response to infection.

words.ex: The temperature today is very high.
words.ex_cn: 今天的温度很高。
words.en: The degree or intensity of heat present in a substance or object, especially as expressed according to a comparative scale and shown by a thermometer or perceived by touch.

words.tr:
n. 咳嗽；
v. 咳嗽；
words.ex: He had a bad cough last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚咳得很厉害。
words.en: A cough is a sudden, forceful expulsion of air from the lungs, often caused by irritation in the airway.

words.tr:
n. 喷嚏；喷嚏声
v. 打喷嚏
words.ex: He had a cold and let out a loud sneeze.
words.ex_cn: 他感冒了，打了一个响亮的喷嚏。
words.en: To sneeze is to suddenly expel air from the nose and mouth due to irritation in the nasal passages.

words.ex: He has insomnia and cannot sleep at night.
words.ex_cn: 他有失眠症，晚上睡不着。
words.en: If someone suffers from insomnia, they find it difficult to sleep.

words.ex: After running for an hour, he felt fatigue.
words.ex_cn: 跑了一个小时后，他感到疲乏。
words.en: A feeling of extreme physical or mental tiredness.

words.tr:
adv. 回原处；向后；
n. 后面；背部；
v. 支持；
adj. 后面的；
words.ex: He put the book back on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 他把书放回了书架。
words.en: The back is the rear surface of the human body from the shoulders to the hips.

words.ex: He feels pain in his lower back after sitting too long.
words.ex_cn: 他坐太久后感到下背部疼痛。
words.en: The part of the back between the ribs and the hips.

words.ex: He hurt his neck while lifting weights.
words.ex_cn: 他在举重时伤了脖子。
words.en: The part of a person's or animal's body connecting the head to the rest of the body.

words.ex: He rubbed his shoulder after lifting the box.
words.ex_cn: 他搬完箱子后揉了揉肩膀。
words.en: The part of the body at each side of the neck where the upper limb or forelimb is attached; to accept or take on (a responsibility or task).

words.ex: He fell and hurt his knee.
words.ex_cn: 他摔倒了，伤了膝盖。
words.en: The knee is the joint between the thigh and the lower leg in humans.

words.ex: He twisted his ankle while running.
words.ex_cn: 他在跑步时扭伤了脚踝。
words.en: The joint between the foot and the leg, in which movement occurs in two planes.

words.tr:
n. 肘部
v. 用肘推挤
words.ex: He hurt his elbow while playing basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他在打篮球时伤了肘部。
words.en: The joint between the forearm and the upper arm; to push someone with your elbow.

words.ex: He hurt his wrist while playing basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他打篮球时伤了手腕。
words.en: The part of your body where your hand joins your arm.

words.tr:
n. 手臂；
v. 武装；
words.ex: He raised his arm to wave hello.
words.ex_cn: 他举起手臂打招呼。
words.en: An arm is one of the two long parts of your body that are attached to your shoulders and that have your hands at the end.

words.ex: He hurt his leg while playing soccer.
words.ex_cn: 他在踢足球时伤了腿。
words.en: A leg is one of the limbs on which a person or animal walks and stands.

words.ex: He rubbed his chest after the cough.
words.ex_cn: 他咳嗽后揉了揉胸部。
words.en: The front part of a person's body between the neck and the stomach, or a large strong box used for storing things.

words.ex: He ate too much and his stomach hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多了，胃疼。
words.en: The stomach is the organ in your body where food is digested after you have eaten it.

words.ex: The old branch can't bend without breaking.
words.ex_cn: 这根老树枝不能弯曲而不折断。

words.tr: phrase. 有限的活动；活动受限
words.ex: The injury caused limited movement in his arm.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤导致他的手臂活动受限。
words.en: Restricted or reduced ability to move a part of the body.

words.tr: phrase. 行走困难；步态障碍
words.ex: She has difficulty walking due to her knee injury.
words.ex_cn: 由于膝盖受伤，她行走困难。
words.en: Difficulty walking refers to the challenge or inability to walk normally, often due to physical or medical conditions.

words.ex: He has difficulty climbing stairs because of his knee pain.
words.ex_cn: 他因为膝盖疼痛而上楼梯困难。
words.en: Challenges or problems when attempting to ascend stairs.

words.ex: He went upstairs to sleep.
words.ex_cn: 他上楼去睡觉了。
words.en: If you go upstairs in a building, you go up a staircase towards a higher floor.

words.ex: He went downstairs to get a drink.
words.ex_cn: 他下楼去拿饮料。
words.en: If you go downstairs in a building, you go down a staircase towards the ground floor.

words.ex: The doctor made a diagnosis after checking the symptoms.
words.ex_cn: 医生在检查了症状后做出了诊断。
words.en: The identification of the nature of an illness or other problem by examination of the symptoms.

words.ex: The doctor did an examination of his arm.
words.ex_cn: 医生对他手臂进行了检查。
words.en: An examination is a formal test that you take to show your knowledge or ability in a particular subject, or to obtain a qualification.

words.ex: He had a check-up at the hospital last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周在医院做了体检。
words.en: A check-up is a medical examination by your doctor to make sure that there is nothing wrong with your health.

words.ex: The doctor used an x-ray to check his bone.
words.ex_cn: 医生用X光检查了他的骨头。
words.en: An X-ray is a type of radiation that can pass through most solid materials. X-rays are used in medicine to make images of the inside of the body.

words.ex: The doctor ordered a blood test to check for any abnormalities.
words.ex_cn: 医生安排了血液检测，以检查是否有任何异常。
words.en: A blood test is a laboratory analysis performed on a blood sample that is usually extracted from a vein in the arm using a hypodermic needle, or via fingerprick. Blood tests are used to determine physiological and biochemical states, such as disease, mineral content, drug effectiveness, and organ function.

words.ex: He scan the QR code with his phone.
words.ex_cn: 他用手机扫描了二维码。
words.en: To look at something carefully or quickly in order to find out specific information or to examine something thoroughly.

words.ex: The doctor gave him proper treatment for the infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他提供了针对感染的适当治疗。
words.en: The act or manner of treating someone or something, especially in a medical context.

words.ex: He is receiving therapy for his back pain.
words.ex_cn: 他正在接受治疗以缓解背痛。
words.en: Therapy is the treatment of someone with mental or physical illness without the use of drugs or operations.

words.ex: He goes to physiotherapy after his surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他手术后去做物理治疗。
words.en: Physiotherapy is the treatment of disease, injury, or deformity by physical methods such as massage, heat treatment, and exercise rather than by drugs or surgery.

words.tr: phrase. 职业治疗；作业疗法（通过有目的的日常活动帮助患者恢复或提高生活、工作能力的一种康复治疗方法）
words.ex: He receives occupational therapy to help with daily tasks.
words.ex_cn: 他接受职业治疗以帮助完成日常任务。
words.en: A type of therapy that helps individuals achieve independence in all facets of their lives, particularly after an injury or illness.

words.tr: n. 药物；药物治疗；药物处理；
words.ex: He took his medication every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃药。
words.en: Medication refers to a substance used for medical treatment, especially a medicine or drug.

words.ex: The doctor prescribed drugs for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他开了治疗头痛的药物。
words.en: A drug is a substance which is used to treat an illness, relieve a symptom, or modify a chemical process in the body for a specific purpose.

words.ex: The doctor wrote a prescription for medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生开了一张药方。
words.en: A prescription is a written order from a physician for the preparation and administration of a drug or device for a patient.

words.ex: He needs surgery for his broken arm.
words.ex_cn: 他需要做手术来治疗断掉的胳膊。
words.en: Surgery is the medical specialty that uses operative manual and instrumental techniques on a patient to investigate or treat a pathological condition such as a disease or injury, to help improve bodily function or appearance, or to repair unwanted ruptured areas.

words.ex: The operation of the machine is very smooth.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器的运行非常顺畅。
words.en: An operation is a planned activity involving many people performing various tasks.

words.ex: The doctor gave him an injection for the pain.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他打了一针来缓解疼痛。
words.en: An injection is the act of putting a liquid, especially a drug, into a person's body using a needle and a syringe.

words.tr:
n. 剩余部分；其他；休息；
v. （使）休息；（使）倚靠；停留在；
words.ex: He ate the first slice and left the rest for his sister.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了第一块，把剩下的留给了他妹妹。
words.en: To rest means to cease work or movement in order to relax, sleep, or recover strength. It can also refer to the remaining part of something.

words.ex: He put an ice pack on his knee after the injury.
words.ex_cn: 他在膝盖受伤后敷了一个冰袋。
words.en: A bag filled with ice or a gel that can be frozen, used to cool an injury or to keep food cold.

words.tr:
n. 绷带
v. 用绷带包扎
words.ex: He put a bandage on his cut finger.
words.ex_cn: 他在他割伤的手指上贴了绷带。
words.en: A bandage is a piece of material used to cover a wound or to support an injured part of the body.

words.ex: The medicine has some side effects.
words.ex_cn: 这种药有一些副作用。
words.en: Unintended effects of a drug or treatment that occur along with the desired effect.

words.tr: n. 药片；平板电脑；石碑；
words.ex: He took two tablets for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了两片药来缓解头痛。
words.en: A tablet is a small, flat piece of medicine that you swallow, or a small, flat computer that is controlled by touching the screen.

words.ex: He takes two pills every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃两粒药丸。
words.en: Small solid round mass of medicine that you swallow without chewing.

words.ex: The medicine comes in small capsules.
words.ex_cn: 这种药装在小容器里。
words.en: A capsule is a small container or a small case, especially one that contains medicine or is used in space travel.

words.ex: The doctor adjusted the dosage of the medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生调整了药物的剂量。
words.en: The amount of a medicine or drug that is taken at one time or over a period of time.

words.tr: n. 练习；锻炼；行使；“exercise”的复数； v. 使用；
words.ex: He does morning exercises every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天做晨练。
words.en: Physical or mental activity that you do to stay healthy or become stronger.

words.ex: He does stretching exercises every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上做拉伸运动。
words.en: Physical activities designed to increase flexibility and muscle length.

words.ex: He does breathing exercises every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上做呼吸练习。
words.en: A series of controlled breathing techniques used to promote relaxation, focus, or physical well-being.

words.ex: He is in rehabilitation after his surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他术后正在康复。
words.en: Rehabilitation is the process of helping someone to have a normal, useful life again after they have been very ill or in prison, or the process of returning a building or area to its previous good condition.

words.ex: He needs time for recovery after the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他手术后需要时间恢复。
words.en: The process of becoming well again after an illness or injury, or the process of returning to a normal condition after a period of difficulty.

words.ex: He works hard to improve his English.
words.ex_cn: 他努力改善自己的英语。
words.en: To make something better, or to become better.

words.tr: n. 拐杖( crutch的名词复数 ); 支持物; 精神上的寄托; 胯部
words.ex: He walked with the aid of crutches.
words.ex_cn: 他借助拐杖行走。
words.en: Crutches are sticks that you put under your arms to help you walk if you have injured your leg or foot.

words.tr:
v. 粘附；（随意）放置；忍受；
n. 棍枝；条状物；球棍；
words.ex: The glue makes the paper stick to the table.
words.ex_cn: 胶水使纸粘在桌子上。
words.en: A stick is a thin branch which has fallen off a tree. If you stick something somewhere, you put it there in a rather casual way.

words.tr: phrase. 手杖；拐杖（用于辅助行走）
words.ex: He uses a walking stick to help him walk.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根拐杖来帮助走路。
words.en: A walking stick is a stick that is used to help someone walk, especially by someone who is old or who has difficulty in walking.

words.tr:
v. 吊起；悬挂；投掷
n. 投掷；悬带
words.ex: The nurse slung the arm in a bandage.
words.ex_cn: 护士用绷带吊起手臂。
words.en: To throw or hurl something with force; to suspend or hang something loosely.

words.tr:
v. 支持；支撑；
n. 拥护；帮助；
words.ex: My friends support me when I feel sad.
words.ex_cn: 当我感到难过时，我的朋友们支持我。
words.en: If you support someone or their ideas or aims, you agree with them, and perhaps help them because you want them to succeed.

words.ex: Handwashing is a simple prevention of disease.
words.ex_cn: 洗手是预防疾病的一种简单方法。
words.en: The act of stopping something from happening or arising.

words.tr: phrase. 热身；变暖；使活跃起来
words.ex: He warms up before running.
words.ex_cn: 他在跑步前热身。
words.en: To prepare for physical exertion or a performance by exercising or practicing gently beforehand.

words.ex: After the game, there is a five-minute cooldown.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后，有一个五分钟的冷却期。

words.ex: He sat with good posture at the desk.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在书桌前，姿势端正。
words.en: Your posture is the way in which you hold your body when you are standing or sitting.

words.tr:
n. 日常饮食；节食；
v. 节制饮食；
words.ex: His diet includes lots of vegetables and fruits.
words.ex_cn: 他的日常饮食包括大量蔬菜和水果。
words.en: The food and drink usually consumed by a person or group; a special course of food to which one restricts oneself, either to lose weight or for medical reasons.

words.tr:
n. 地址；演讲；
v. 解决；向…讲话；
words.ex: Please write your address on the form.
words.ex_cn: 请把你的地址写在表格上。
words.en: The particulars of the place where someone lives or an organization is situated; a formal speech delivered to an audience.

words.ex: I appreciate the beauty of nature.
words.ex_cn: 我欣赏大自然的美。
words.en: If you appreciate something, you recognize its value and feel grateful for it.

words.tr:
n. （长篇）小说；
adj. 新颖的；新奇的；
words.ex: He wrote a novel about a brave girl.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一部关于一个勇敢女孩的小说。
words.en: A novel is a long written story about imaginary people and events.

words.ex: This sentence is easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 这个句子很容易理解。
words.en: A sentence is a group of words which, when they are written down, begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop, question mark, or exclamation mark. Most sentences contain a subject and a verb.

words.tr:
n. 大学毕业生；
v. 毕业；
words.ex: He is a graduate of Harvard University.
words.ex_cn: 他是哈佛大学的毕业生。
words.en: A graduate is a person who has successfully completed a degree at a university or college and has received a certificate or diploma stating this. To graduate means to successfully complete a degree at a university or college.

words.tr:
n. 纪律；学科；科目；训练；惩戒；
v. 约束自己；
words.ex: The teacher enforced discipline in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 老师在教室里维持纪律。
words.en: Discipline is the practice of making people obey rules or standards of behaviour, and punishing them when they do not.

words.ex: The car consumes a lot of gas.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车消耗很多汽油。
words.en: To consume something means to eat or drink it, or to use it up in some way.

words.ex: He works in the tech industry.
words.ex_cn: 他在科技行业工作。
words.en: Industry is the work and processes involved in collecting raw materials, and making them into products in factories.

words.tr:
n. 教练；长途客运汽车；
v. 训练；培训；
words.ex: The coach taught the team how to win.
words.ex_cn: 教练教球队如何获胜。
words.en: A coach is someone who trains a person or team in a particular sport. It also refers to a large, comfortable bus that carries passengers on long journeys.

words.ex: You need to pay a 40-yuan deposit to rent the bike.
words.ex_cn: 租自行车需要支付40元押金。
words.en: A deposit is a sum of money which is part of the full price of something, and which you pay when you agree to buy it. It is also a sum of money that you pay into a bank account.

words.ex: I made a reservation for two at the restaurant.
words.ex_cn: 我在餐厅预订了两个人的座位。
words.en: A reservation is an arrangement whereby something, especially a seat or room, is kept for a particular person who will arrive later.

words.ex: Spring is a beautiful season.
words.ex_cn: 春天是一个美丽的季节。
words.en: A season is one of the four periods of the year: spring, summer, autumn, or winter. It can also refer to a period of the year characterized by particular conditions of weather, temperature, etc., or a period of the year when a particular sport is played.

words.tr: n. 设施；特色功能；特定场所；资质；
words.ex: The school has a new sports facility.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校有一个新的体育设施。
words.en: A facility is a place, building, or service that is designed for a particular purpose.

words.tr: n. 定居点；定居（过程）；协议；
words.ex: The small settlement near the river has five houses.
words.ex_cn: 河边的小定居点有五所房子。
words.en: A settlement is an official agreement intended to resolve a dispute or conflict.

words.ex: She put the food on a clean plate.
words.ex_cn: 她把食物放在一个干净的盘子里。
words.en: A flat dish, typically circular and made of china, from which food is eaten or served.

words.tr:
adj. 当前的；流通的；
n. （水、气、电）流；趋势；
words.ex: The current weather is very hot.
words.ex_cn: 当前的天气非常热。
words.en: belonging to the present time; happening or being used or done now

words.tr: n. 群体；殖民地；聚居地；
words.ex: A colony of ants moved quickly across the ground.
words.ex_cn: 一群蚂蚁迅速从地上爬过。
words.en: A colony is a country or area that is under the political control of another country, usually one that is far away, and where people from that country live.

words.ex: The remote needs a new battery.
words.ex_cn: 遥控器需要新电池。
words.en: A battery is a device that produces electricity to provide power for radios, cars, toys, etc.

words.ex: I love learning about different cultures.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢了解不同的文化。
words.en: The ideas, customs, and social behavior of a particular people or society.

words.ex: Farmers grow grain like wheat and rice.
words.ex_cn: 农民种植小麦和大米等谷物。
words.en: A grain is a small, hard seed of a food plant such as wheat, rice, or corn, or the plant itself.

words.ex: I need to recharge my phone.
words.ex_cn: 我需要给我的手机再充电。
words.en: To charge a battery or device again; to regain energy or vitality.

words.ex: His argument was clear and logical.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点清晰而有逻辑。
words.en: An argument is a discussion or debate in which people express different opinions about something.

words.tr:
n. 暴躁脾气；情绪；心情；性情
v. 使…缓和；冲淡
words.ex: He loses his temper when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，他会发脾气。
words.en: If you refer to someone's temper or say that they have a temper, you mean that they become angry very easily.

words.ex: He became the champion of the tennis tournament.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得了网球锦标赛的冠军。
words.en: A champion is someone who has won first prize in a competition, contest, or fight.

words.tr:
v. 阻碍；妨碍
n. （带盖）篮子
words.ex: Rain hampered our picnic plans.
words.ex_cn: 雨妨碍了我们的野餐计划。
words.en: If something hampers you, it makes it difficult for you to do something.

words.tr:
n. 总计；集合体
adj. 合计的；总的
v. （使）聚集；聚合；总计为
words.ex: The aggregate of all sales this month is $50,000.
words.ex_cn: 本月所有销售额的总计是5万美元。
words.en: An aggregate is a number of things or people that are considered as a group or a whole.

words.tr: n. 位置；职位；地位；姿势；
words.ex: The book is on the table in a good position.
words.ex_cn: 书放在桌子上的一个好位置。
words.en: A position refers to the place or type of role someone has in a situation, organization, or society, or the way in which someone or something is placed or arranged.

words.tr:
n. 邮件；职位；邮寄；帖子；柱；
v. 邮寄；张贴；
words.ex: I checked the post this morning.
words.ex_cn: 我今天早上检查了邮件。
words.en: To post something means to send it through the postal system or to display it publicly, such as on a noticeboard or the internet. It can also refer to the act of assigning someone to a particular job or position.

words.ex: There is a vacancy in the sales department.
words.ex_cn: 销售部门有一个空缺职位。
words.en: A vacancy is a position or job that is available for someone to fill.

words.ex: He played the role of a teacher in the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他在电影中扮演了老师的角色。
words.en: The function or position that someone has in a particular situation or activity.

words.ex: He got a new job last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周找到了一份新工作。
words.en: A job is the work that someone does regularly in order to earn money.

words.tr: n. 开始；开口；空缺职位； v. 打开；“open”的现在分词； adj. 开始的；
words.ex: The opening of the meeting was delayed.
words.ex_cn: 会议的开始被推迟了。
words.en: An opening is a gap or hole in something, or the act of making or becoming open. It can also refer to the beginning of an event or period.

words.tr: phrase. 志愿者职位；义务工作职位
words.ex: He applied for a volunteer position at the animal shelter.
words.ex_cn: 他申请了动物收容所的志愿者职位。

words.ex: The teacher has an assistant to help with grading.
words.ex_cn: 老师有一个助理帮忙批改作业。
words.en: An assistant is a person who helps in particular work or who is under the authority of another person.

words.ex: The receptionist greeted the visitors with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 接待员微笑着迎接了访客。
words.en: A receptionist is a person whose job is to deal with people arriving at or telephoning a hotel, office building, doctor's surgery, etc.

words.ex: My tutor helps me with math homework.
words.ex_cn: 我的导师帮我做数学作业。
words.en: A tutor is someone who gives private lessons to one pupil or a very small group of pupils.

words.ex: The clerk at the store helped me find the book.
words.ex_cn: 商店里的职员帮我找到了那本书。
words.en: A clerk is a person whose job is to keep records or accounts in an office, shop, or bank.

words.ex: The supervisor checked the workers' progress.
words.ex_cn: 主管检查了工人们的进展。
words.en: A supervisor is a person who oversees and directs the work of others.

words.ex: The caretaker cleans the building every day.
words.ex_cn: 看管人每天打扫这座大楼。
words.en: A caretaker is a person whose job is to look after a large building such as a school or a block of flats or apartments, and deal with small repairs to it.

words.ex: He got a teaching qualification last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年获得了教师资格。
words.en: A qualification is a skill or type of experience that you need in order to do a particular job or activity.

words.tr: n. 需求；要求；必要条件；
words.ex: The job has a requirement of two years of experience.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作的要求是两年经验。
words.en: A requirement is something that is necessary or that must be done.

words.tr: n. 标准；尺度；准则；“criterion”的复数；
words.ex: The main criteria for selection are skill and experience.
words.ex_cn: 选择的主要标准是技能和经验。
words.en: A criterion is a standard or principle by which something is judged or decided.

words.ex: He received a certificate for completing the course.
words.ex_cn: 他完成了课程后获得了证书。
words.en: A certificate is an official document attesting a fact, in particular.

words.tr: n. 毕业文凭；学位证书；
words.ex: He received his diploma last June.
words.ex_cn: 他去年六月拿到了毕业文凭。
words.en: A diploma is a document which may be awarded by a university or college, or by a high school, showing that someone has successfully completed a course of study.

words.ex: The temperature is 30 degrees today.
words.ex_cn: 今天气温是30度。
words.en: A degree is a unit of measurement for angles, or a qualification given to a student by a college or university after they have completed a course of study.

words.tr:
n. 经验；阅历；
v. 经历；体验；
words.ex: He has a lot of experience in teaching English.
words.ex_cn: 他有丰富的英语教学经验。
words.en: Experience is knowledge or skill in a particular job or activity that you have gained because you have done that job or activity for a long time.

words.ex: He learned cooking skill from his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他从妈妈那里学到了烹饪技能。
words.en: An ability to do something well, especially because you have learned and practiced it.

words.ex: The availability of free Wi-Fi is important for travelers.
words.ex_cn: 免费Wi-Fi的可用性对旅行者很重要。
words.en: The quality of being able to be used or obtained.

words.ex: His nationality is Canadian.
words.ex_cn: 他的国籍是加拿大人。
words.en: Nationality is the legal relationship between an individual and a state, often used to refer to the country to which a person belongs.

words.ex: His date of birth is June 5, 2000.
words.ex_cn: 他的出生日期是2000年6月5日。
words.en: The day, month, and year on which someone was born.

words.ex: He filled out his current employment status on the form.
words.ex_cn: 他在表格上填写了自己的当前就业状况。

words.ex: He does exercise every day to improve his physical fitness.
words.ex_cn: 他每天锻炼以提高身体健康。
words.en: The condition of being physically healthy and strong, especially as a result of exercise and proper nutrition.

words.tr: phrase. 良好的视力；视觉敏锐
words.ex: He has good eyesight and can read small letters.
words.ex_cn: 他视力很好，能看清小字。
words.en: The ability to see well, without the need for glasses or contact lenses.

words.ex: He has color blindness and cannot tell red from green.
words.ex_cn: 他有色盲，无法分辨红色和绿色。
words.en: Color blindness is the inability or decreased ability to see color, or perceive color differences, under normal lighting conditions.

words.ex: He has colour blindness and cannot tell red from green.
words.ex_cn: 他有色盲，无法分辨红色和绿色。
words.en: Colour blindness is the inability or decreased ability to see colour, or perceive colour differences, under normal lighting conditions.

words.ex: He has an allergy to peanuts.
words.ex_cn: 他对花生过敏。
words.en: An allergy is a condition in which your immune system reacts abnormally to a foreign substance.

words.ex: He got his driver's license last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周拿到了驾照。
words.en: An official document permitting a person to drive a motor vehicle.

words.ex: He got his driving licence last month.
words.ex_cn: 他上个月拿到了驾照。
words.en: A driving licence is an official document permitting a specific individual to operate one or more types of motorized vehicles on public roads.

words.ex: He wants to apply for a job at the library.
words.ex_cn: 他想申请图书馆的工作。
words.en: To make a formal request, usually in writing, for something such as a job, a place at a university, or permission to do something.

words.ex: He submitted his application for the job last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周提交了那份工作申请。
words.en: An application is a formal request, often written, for something such as a job, a place at a university, or permission to do something. It can also refer to the act of putting something to a special use or purpose, or a program or piece of software designed to perform a specific function.

words.ex: He will submit his homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会提交他的作业。
words.en: To yield or surrender (oneself) to the will or authority of another.

words.tr:
n. 最后候选人名单
v. 把 ... 列入最后候选人名单
words.ex: They shortlisted five candidates for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他们为这份工作筛选出五名候选人。
words.en: A shortlist is a list of selected candidates from which a final choice is made.

words.tr:
n. 面试；访谈；
v. 面试；接见；
words.ex: He has an interview tomorrow for a new job.
words.ex_cn: 他明天有一场新工作的面试。
words.en: An interview is a formal meeting at which someone is asked questions in order to find out if they are suitable for a job or a course of study.

words.tr:
v. 提供；
n. 提供；提议；报价；
words.ex: He offers help to his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他向同学提供帮助。
words.en: If you offer something to someone, you ask them if they would like to have it or use it.

words.tr:
n. 合同；契约；
v. 收缩；
words.ex: They signed a contract to buy the house.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一份购买房子的合同。
words.en: A contract is a legal agreement between two or more parties. It can also mean to become smaller or tighter, or to catch a disease.

words.tr: abbr. 简历；履历；“curriculum vitae”的缩写
words.ex: He sent his cv to the company.
words.ex_cn: 他把简历发给了公司。
words.en: A document that summarizes a person's education, work experience, and other qualifications for a job.

words.ex: After a short break, he resumed his work.
words.ex_cn: 短暂休息后，他继续工作。
words.en: If you resume an activity or if it resumes, it begins again or continues after an interruption.

words.tr: n. 参考；提及；介绍信；引用；
words.ex: Please use this book for reference.
words.ex_cn: 请使用这本书作为参考。
words.en: A reference is a mention of something or someone, or a letter or statement about someone's character or abilities.

words.tr: phrase. 求职信；附函（随简历或文件一同寄出的说明信）
words.ex: He wrote a cover letter for his job application.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的工作申请写了一封求职信。
words.en: A cover letter is a document sent with your resume to provide additional information on your skills and experience. The letter typically provides detailed information on why you are qualified for the job you are applying for.

words.ex: He showed his portfolio to the art teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他向美术老师展示了他作品集。
words.en: A portfolio is a set of pictures by someone, or photographs of examples of their work, which they use when entering competitions or applying for work.

words.ex: He took a passport photo at the studio.
words.ex_cn: 他在照相馆拍了一张护照照片。
words.en: A photograph that is required for official documents such as passports.

words.tr: abbr. 身份证明；“ identification”的缩写
words.ex: He forgot his id at home.
words.ex_cn: 他把身份证忘在家里了。
words.en: In psychoanalytic theory, the id is the part of the mind in which innate instinctive impulses and primary processes are manifest.

words.ex: He needs a visa to travel to Japan.
words.ex_cn: 他需要一张签证去日本旅行。
words.en: A visa is an official document, or a stamp put in your passport, which allows you to enter or leave a particular country.

words.ex: He gets a salary of 3000 dollars each month.
words.ex_cn: 他每个月赚3000美元的工资。
words.en: A salary is the money that someone is paid each month by their employer, especially when they are in a profession such as teaching, law, or medicine.

words.ex: He receives his wage every Friday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周五领工资。
words.en: A wage is the money that someone is paid each week by their employer, especially for manual or unskilled work. To wage means to carry on (a war or campaign).

words.tr: phrase. 工资率；薪酬标准；每小时/每单位工作的报酬
words.ex: His pay rate is $15 per hour.
words.ex_cn: 他的工资是每小时15美元。
words.en: The amount of money paid per unit of time or work performed.

words.tr: n. 奖金；红利；额外津贴；
words.ex: He received a bonus for working overtime.
words.ex_cn: 他因加班获得了奖金。
words.en: A bonus is an extra amount of money that is added to someone's pay, usually because they have worked very hard.

words.ex: My parents give me a weekly allowance.
words.ex_cn: 我父母每周给我零用钱。
words.en: An allowance is money that is given regularly, usually to a child, by their parents, or by the government to someone who is unemployed or ill.

words.tr: n. 利益；好处；“benefit”的复数； v. 有益于；有助于；
words.ex: The benefits of exercise are clear.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼的好处是显而易见的。
words.en: Benefits are advantages or profits that you get from something, especially advantages that you get from the government or from your employer, such as money or health insurance.

words.tr:
n. 转移；移位；转变；轮班；
v. 变换位置；转移；换（挡）；轮班；
words.ex: The shift of power to the new government was sudden.
words.ex_cn: 权力向新政府的转移是突然的。
words.en: If you shift something or if it shifts, it moves or changes its position slightly. If someone's opinion, attitude, or behaviour shifts, it changes slightly, especially in response to a particular situation or event.

words.tr: adj. 全部时间的；专任的
words.ex: He works full-time at a grocery store.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家杂货店全职工作。
words.en: If you are a full-time worker, you work the normal number of hours or days in a week.

words.tr: adj. 兼职的；部分时间的
words.ex: He works part-time at a coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家咖啡店做兼职。
words.en: If someone is a part-time worker or has a part-time job, they work for only part of each day or week.

words.tr: phrase. 灵活的工作时间；可变动的上班时间
words.ex: He works with flexible hours to balance his family time.
words.ex_cn: 他工作时间灵活，以便平衡家庭时间。
words.en: A work schedule that allows employees to vary their arrival and/or departure times.

words.ex: He worked overtime to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 他加班完成了这个项目。
words.en: Overtime refers to the time worked beyond one's regular working hours, often with additional pay.

words.ex: The location of the store is near the park.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店的位置在公园附近。
words.en: A location is the place where something happens or is situated.

words.ex: The tree has many branches.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树有许多分支。
words.en: A branch of a tree is one of its parts that grows out from its trunk. A branch of a business or organization is one of its offices or shops that are in different places.

words.ex: The head office is in New York.
words.ex_cn: 总部在纽约。
words.en: The main office or center of control of a business or organization, where the most important decisions are made.

words.ex: The induction of the new mayor will be held next Monday.
words.ex_cn: 新市长的就职典礼将在下周一举行。
words.en: Induction is the process or action of inducting someone to a position or organization, or the process of reasoning from specific cases to general rules.

words.tr: n. 入学介绍；岗前训练；方向；取向；
words.ex: The school held an orientation for new students on Monday.
words.ex_cn: 学校在周一为新生举行了入学介绍。
words.en: The act of orienting or the state of being oriented; the determination of the relative position of something or someone (especially oneself).

words.ex: She was offered a job with a three-month trial period.
words.ex_cn: 她被提供了一份为期三个月的试用期工作。
words.en: A trial period is a length of time during which someone is tested or tried out in a new job or situation.

words.ex: He is on probation for one year.
words.ex_cn: 他被判缓刑一年。
words.en: Probation is a period of time during which someone who has committed a crime has to behave well and not commit any more crimes in order to avoid being sent to prison.

words.tr:
adj. 一致的；统一的；
n. 制服；
words.ex: The students wear a uniform shirt to school.
words.ex_cn: 学生们穿一致的衬衫去学校。
words.en: A uniform is a special set of clothes which some people, for example soldiers or the police, wear to work in and which some children wear at school. It is also used to describe something that is the same in all parts and does not vary.

words.ex: The juniper tree is known for its aromatic berries.
words.ex_cn: 杜松树以其芳香的浆果而闻名。
words.en: A juniper is an evergreen shrub or small tree that has small, needle-like leaves and produces berry-like cones. It is often used for flavoring gin and in traditional medicine.

words.ex: The fungus grows on old trees.
words.ex_cn: 真菌生长在老树上。
words.en: A fungus is a simple type of plant that has no leaves or flowers and that grows on plants or decaying matter.

words.ex: The garden is full of flowering plants in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天，花园里开满了开花植物。
words.en: A flowering plant is any plant that produces flowers, fruits, and seeds, belonging to the group Angiospermae.

words.ex: He picked a red berry from the bush.
words.ex_cn: 他从灌木丛中摘了一颗红色浆果。
words.en: A berry is a small, round fruit that grows on a bush or a tree. Some berries are edible and can be eaten raw or used in cooking.

words.tr:
n. 种子；籽；
v. 播种；
words.ex: The farmer planted the seed in the soil.
words.ex_cn: 农夫把种子种在土里。
words.en: A seed is the small, hard part of a plant from which a new plant grows.

words.ex: The gardener planted a seedling in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 园丁在花园里种了一株幼苗。
words.en: A seedling is a young plant that has grown from a seed.

words.tr: n. 切割；剪辑； v. 削减；切；割；“cut”的现在分词； adj. 锐利的；
words.ex: The cutting of the tree took only five minutes.
words.ex_cn: 砍树的切割只用了五分钟。
words.en: The act or process of cutting something; a piece cut off from something, especially a plant.

words.tr:
n. 树皮；
v. 狗吠；
words.ex: The dog climbed the tree and touched the bark.
words.ex_cn: 狗爬上了树，摸了摸树皮。
words.en: The sound a dog makes; the outer covering of a tree.

words.tr:
n. 根；根源；
v. 生根；
words.ex: The root of 9 is 3.
words.ex_cn: 9的平方根是3。
words.en: The root of a plant is the part that grows underground and absorbs water and minerals. It can also refer to the origin or cause of something.

words.ex: The tree has many branches.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树有许多分支。
words.en: A branch of a tree is one of its parts that grows out from its trunk. A branch of a business or organization is one of its offices or shops that are in different places.

words.ex: Bees help with pollination of flowers.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂帮助花朵授粉。
words.en: The transfer of pollen from an anther to a stigma; thereby enabling fertilization and sexual reproduction in plants.

words.ex: This forest has many different species of birds.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林有多种不同的鸟类物种。
words.en: A species is a class of plants or animals whose members have the same main characteristics and are able to breed with each other.

words.tr: n. 栖息地；居留地；产地；
words.ex: The panda's habitat is in the mountains of China.
words.ex_cn: 熊猫的栖息地在中国的山区。
words.en: The natural environment in which a species or group of species lives.

words.ex: The forest is a healthy ecosystem.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林是一个健康的生态系统。
words.en: An ecosystem is a complex network or interconnected system, especially one that involves a community of living organisms in conjunction with their environment.

words.ex: Britain colonised many parts of Africa.
words.ex_cn: 英国在非洲许多地区建立了殖民地。
words.en: To colonise means to send people to live in and govern another country, or to take control of an area and send people to live there.

words.ex: They established a new school in the village.
words.ex_cn: 他们在村里建立了一所新学校。
words.en: To set up or create something, such as an organization or a system, on a firm or permanent basis.

words.tr:
adj. 本土的；
n. 土著；本地人；
words.ex: This plant is native to Australia.
words.ex_cn: 这种植物原产于澳大利亚。
words.en: A native of a particular country or region is someone who was born in that country or region.

words.ex: The indigenous people live in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 本土居民住在森林里。
words.en: Indigenous people or things belong to the country in which they are found, rather than coming there or being brought there from another country.

words.tr: phrase. 入侵物种；外来入侵物种（指被引入非原生地并对当地生态系统造成危害的生物种类）
words.ex: The invasive species spread quickly and hurt local plants.
words.ex_cn: 这些入侵物种迅速蔓延，伤害了本地植物。
words.en: An invasive species is a species that is not native to a specific location (an introduced species), and that has a tendency to spread to a degree believed to cause damage to the environment, human economy or human health.

words.tr: phrase. 外来物种；外来的生物种类，指原产于其他地区而被引入到新环境中的动植物或微生物
words.ex: The alien species spread quickly in the new environment.
words.ex_cn: 这种外来物种在新环境中迅速蔓延。
words.en: An alien species refers to a species that is not native to a specific location and has been introduced either accidentally or deliberately by human activities.

words.ex: Bees are important pollinators for flowers.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂是花朵的重要传粉者。
words.en: A pollinator is an animal that moves pollen from the male part of a flower to the female part of a flower, thus enabling fertilization and the production of seeds.

words.ex: Bees and flowers have symbiosis.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂和花朵之间有共生关系。
words.en: Symbiosis is a close relationship between two different kinds of living things in which each provides something that the other needs.

words.ex: A dog is a mammal.
words.ex_cn: 狗是一种哺乳动物。
words.en: A mammal is a type of animal that feeds its young with milk produced by the mother's body. Mammals are warm-blooded and usually have hair or fur.

words.ex: The bird flies over the tree.
words.ex_cn: 鸟飞过树。
words.en: A bird is a creature with feathers and wings. Female birds lay eggs, and most birds can fly.

words.ex: The insect flew over the grass.
words.ex_cn: 那只昆虫飞过了草地。
words.en: An insect is a small animal that has six legs. Most insects have wings. Ants, flies, butterflies, and beetles are all insects.

words.ex: A snake is a reptile.
words.ex_cn: 蛇是一种爬行动物。
words.en: A reptile is a cold-blooded vertebrate of the class Reptilia, including snakes, lizards, crocodiles, turtles, and tortoises. They are characterized by their scaly skin and the fact that they lay eggs on land.

words.tr: n. 掠夺者；捕食性动物；食肉动物；
words.ex: The lion is a predator that hunts deer.
words.ex_cn: 狮子是一种捕食鹿的掠夺者。
words.en: A predator is an animal that naturally preys on others.

words.tr:
n. 猎物；受害者；受骗者；
v. 捕食；坑害；折磨；
words.ex: The lion chased its prey across the plain.
words.ex_cn: 狮子在平原上追逐它的猎物。
words.en: An animal that is hunted and killed by another for food.

words.ex: The sexes have different roles in some traditional societies.
words.ex_cn: 在一些传统社会中，两性有不同的角色。

words.ex: Birds begin migration in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类在秋天开始迁徙。
words.en: The movement of people, animals, or birds from one place to another, especially regularly according to the seasons.

words.ex: Bears go into hibernation in winter.
words.ex_cn: 熊在冬天冬眠。
words.en: Hibernation is a state of inactivity and metabolic depression in endotherms during winter.

words.tr: n. 群体；殖民地；聚居地；
words.ex: A colony of ants moved quickly across the ground.
words.ex_cn: 一群蚂蚁迅速从地上爬过。
words.en: A colony is a country or area that is under the political control of another country, usually one that is far away, and where people from that country live.

words.ex: Pandas are endangered species.
words.ex_cn: 熊猫是濒危物种。
words.en: An endangered species is a type of organism that is at risk of extinction due to a rapid decrease in its population or a loss of its critical habitat.

words.tr: phrase. 受威胁物种；指因栖息地丧失、气候变化、过度捕猎等原因而面临灭绝风险的动植物种类
words.ex: The panda is a threatened species.
words.ex_cn: 熊猫是一种濒危物种。
words.en: A threatened species is a species that is vulnerable to extinction in the near future.

words.ex: Bacteria can make you sick.
words.ex_cn: 细菌会让你生病。
words.en: Bacteria are very small organisms. Some bacteria can cause diseases.

words.ex: The virus made many people sick.
words.ex_cn: 这个病毒让很多人病了。
words.en: A virus is a very small organism that causes infectious diseases in people, animals, and plants.

words.ex: The wound caused a serious infection.
words.ex_cn: 伤口引起了严重的感染。
words.en: An infection is a disease caused by microorganisms such as bacteria, viruses, or parasites invading the body.

words.tr: adj. 传染性的；有感染力的；
words.ex: The flu is contagious and spreads easily.
words.ex_cn: 流感具有传染性，容易传播。
words.en: A contagious disease can be caught by touching someone who has the disease or by touching an infected object or by breathing in infected air.

words.tr: adj. 传染性的；有感染力的；
words.ex: The virus is infectious and spreads quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒具有传染性，传播迅速。
words.en: An infectious disease can be passed from one person to another, especially through the air they breathe.

words.ex: The epidemic spread quickly across the country.
words.ex_cn: 这种流行病迅速蔓延到全国。
words.en: An epidemic is a large number of cases of an infectious disease occurring at the same time.

words.ex: The immune system fights germs in the body.
words.ex_cn: 免疫系统在体内对抗细菌。
words.en: The immune system is the body's defense against infectious organisms and other invaders. Through a series of steps called the immune response, the immune system attacks organisms and substances that invade body systems and cause disease.

words.tr: n. 寄生虫；寄生生物；依赖他人过活者；
words.ex: The parasite lives inside the host's body.
words.ex_cn: 这种寄生虫生活在宿主的体内。
words.en: A parasite is an organism that lives on or in a host organism and gets its food from or at the expense of its host.

words.ex: The extinction of dinosaurs happened millions of years ago.
words.ex_cn: 恐龙的灭绝发生在数百万年前。
words.en: The state or process of a species, family, or larger group being or becoming extinct.

words.tr: phrase. v. 灭绝；消失；不复存在
words.ex: The dinosaur became extinct millions of years ago.
words.ex_cn: 恐龙在数百万年前灭绝了。
words.en: To no longer exist or to die out completely.

words.tr: phrase. 栖息地丧失；生态环境被破坏导致生物无法生存的现象
words.ex: Animals lose their homes because of habitat loss.
words.ex_cn: 动物因为栖息地丧失而失去了家园。
words.en: The destruction or degradation of the natural environment in which a particular species lives, leading to a reduction in the available habitat and often resulting in a decline in population or extinction.

words.tr: n. 毁灭；引起毁灭的根源；
words.ex: The storm caused the destruction of the village.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴摧毁了村庄。
words.en: The act of destroying something, or the state of being destroyed.

words.tr: n. 采伐森林；森林开伐；
words.ex: Deforestation is killing many animals.
words.ex_cn: 采伐森林正在杀死许多动物。
words.en: The act of cutting down or burning all the trees in an area.

words.tr: phrase. 生物多样性丧失；指物种、基因和生态系统多样性的减少
words.ex: Deforestation causes biodiversity loss.
words.ex_cn: 砍伐森林导致生物多样性丧失。
words.en: The decrease in the variety and variability of life on Earth, including the extinction of species, the loss of genetic diversity within species, and the destruction of ecosystems.

words.ex: Climate change is making the weather hotter.
words.ex_cn: 气候变化让天气变得更热。
words.en: A significant and lasting change in the Earth's climate, especially a change due to an increase in the average atmospheric temperature.

words.ex: Global warming is making the Earth hotter.
words.ex_cn: 全球变暖正在让地球变得更热。
words.en: Global warming refers to the long-term increase in Earth's average surface temperature due to human activities, primarily fossil fuel burning, which increases heat-trapping greenhouse gas levels in Earth's atmosphere.

words.ex: The river is dirty because of pollution.
words.ex_cn: 这条河因为污染而变得肮脏。
words.en: Pollution is the process of making air, water, soil, etc. dirty and not safe or suitable to use.

words.ex: Overfishing is hurting the ocean fish.
words.ex_cn: 过度捕捞正在伤害海洋中的鱼类。
words.en: The act of catching too many fish at once, so that the fish population becomes too low to recover.

words.tr: n. 过度捕猎；过度狩猎
words.ex: Overhunting killed many wild animals.
words.ex_cn: 过度捕猎导致许多野生动物死亡。
words.en: The excessive hunting of animals, leading to population decline or extinction.

words.tr: n. 保护；节约（自然资源）；
words.ex: The park is for the conservation of wild animals.
words.ex_cn: 这个公园是为了保护野生动物。
words.en: The protection and preservation of the natural environment and wildlife.

words.ex: The museum focuses on the preservation of old books.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆专注于旧书的保存。
words.en: The act of keeping something in its original state or in good condition.

words.ex: The animals live in a protected area.
words.ex_cn: 这些动物生活在一个保护区里。
words.en: A protected area is a clearly defined geographical space, recognized, dedicated and managed, through legal or other effective means, to achieve the long-term conservation of nature with associated ecosystem services and cultural values.

words.ex: The birds live in a nature reserve.
words.ex_cn: 这些鸟生活在自然保护区。
words.en: A nature reserve is a protected area of importance for wildlife, flora, fauna or features of geological or other special interest, which is reserved and managed for conservation and to provide special opportunities for study or research.

words.tr: phrase. 繁殖计划；育种项目（指为改良动植物品种而系统地进行交配和培育的计划）
words.ex: The zoo has started a breeding program to save the endangered species.
words.ex_cn: 动物园启动了一项育种计划来拯救濒危物种。
words.en: A breeding program is a planned series of actions aimed at breeding animals or plants, especially to produce a new or improved variety.

words.ex: The reintroduction of wolves helped balance the forest ecosystem.
words.ex_cn: 狼的再引入帮助平衡了森林生态系统。
words.en: The act of introducing something again, especially a species of animal or plant into an area where it has become extinct or rare.

words.ex: The restoration of the old house took two years.
words.ex_cn: 这座老房子的修复花了两年时间。
words.en: The act of returning something to its original condition, or the state of being returned to its original condition.

words.tr: phrase. 可持续的使用；指在不损害环境或资源再生能力的前提下对自然资源的利用
words.ex: We must practice sustainable use of water.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须合理使用水资源。
words.en: The use of resources in a way that does not deplete them for future generations.

words.tr:
n. 避难所；庇护所；
v. 庇护；遮蔽；
words.ex: The refugees found shelter in a small building.
words.ex_cn: 难民们在一个小建筑里找到了避难所。
words.en: A shelter is a small building or covered place which is made to protect people from bad weather or danger.

words.ex: The new legislation bans plastic bags.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法规禁止使用塑料袋。
words.en: Legislation refers to the process of making or enacting laws by a government or other authority.

words.ex: He broke the law and was arrested.
words.ex_cn: 他违反了法律，被逮捕了。
words.en: A law is a rule or set of rules for good behaviour which is considered right and important by the majority of people for moral, religious, or emotional reasons.

words.ex: The campaign increased public awareness about recycling.
words.ex_cn: 这个活动提高了公众对回收利用的意识。
words.en: Public awareness refers to the general level of consciousness or understanding among the public about a particular issue or topic.

words.tr:
n. 低地；
adj. 低地的；
words.ex: The farmers live in the lowland near the river.
words.ex_cn: 农民们住在河边的低地上。
words.en: Lowland refers to an area of land that is low in relation to the surrounding country.

words.ex: The sheep graze on the highland.
words.ex_cn: 羊在高地上吃草。
words.en: Highland refers to an area of high or mountainous land, often characterized by its elevation above sea level and distinct geographical features.

words.ex: The children saw a big rainforest on their trip.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在旅行中看到了一片热带雨林。
words.en: A dense, tropical forest that receives a high amount of rainfall, typically located near the equator.

words.ex: Monkeys live in the tropical forest.
words.ex_cn: 猴子生活在热带雨林中。
words.en: A forest located in a region with a hot, humid climate.

words.ex: The wetland is home to many birds.
words.ex_cn: 这片湿地是许多鸟类的家园。
words.en: Wetlands are areas where water covers the soil, or is present either at or near the surface of the soil all year or for varying periods of time during the year, including during the growing season.

words.ex: The birds live in a quiet marsh.
words.ex_cn: 这些鸟生活在一片宁静的沼泽中。
words.en: A marsh is an area of low-lying land which is flooded in wet seasons or at high tide, and typically remains waterlogged at all times.

words.ex: The swamp is full of tall grass and frogs.
words.ex_cn: 这个沼泽里长满了高草和青蛙。
words.en: A swamp is an area of low-lying, uncultivated ground where water collects; a bog or marsh.

words.ex: The cows graze on the grassland.
words.ex_cn: 牛在牧场上吃草。
words.en: Grassland is a large open area of country covered with grass, especially one used for grazing.

words.ex: Lions live in the savanna.
words.ex_cn: 狮子生活在热带大草原上。
words.en: A savanna is a grassy plain in tropical and subtropical regions, with few trees.

words.tr: phrase. 沿海地区；海岸区域
words.ex: The fishers live in a small coastal area.
words.ex_cn: 渔民们住在一个小的沿海地区。
words.en: A coastal area is a region that is near the sea. It often features beaches, cliffs, or other landforms that are directly adjacent to the ocean.

words.tr: n. 海（或湖）滨线；海（或湖）岸线
words.ex: The children played near the shoreline.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在岸边玩耍。
words.en: The line where a body of water meets the land.

words.ex: The temperate zone has four clear seasons.
words.ex_cn: 温带地区有四个明显的季节。
words.en: The temperate zones are the parts of the Earth's surface that lie between the tropics and the polar circles. These areas experience moderate temperatures and distinct seasons.

words.ex: The river basin provides water for many villages.
words.ex_cn: 河流流域为许多村庄提供水源。
words.en: The area of land drained by a river and its tributaries.

words.tr: n. 分水岭；集水区；转折点
words.ex: The river forms a watershed between two valleys.
words.ex_cn: 这条河构成了两个山谷之间的分水岭。
words.en: A watershed is an event or period that is important because it represents a big change in how people do or think about something.

words.ex: The ice age covered big parts of the Earth with ice.
words.ex_cn: 冰河时代使地球的大部分地区被冰覆盖。
words.en: A period in the Earth's history when ice sheets covered large areas of the planet's surface.

words.tr: phrase. 地质年代；地质时期
words.ex: The dinosaur era belongs to a geological period called the Mesozoic.
words.ex_cn: 恐龙时代属于一个叫做中生代的地质年代。

words.ex: The invention of the internet changed our era.
words.ex_cn: 互联网的发明改变了我们的时代。
words.en: An era is a period of time that is considered as a single unit because of a particular characteristic or event.

words.ex: The ancient Egyptians built the pyramids.
words.ex_cn: 古埃及人建造了金字塔。
words.en: Belonging to the very distant past and no longer in existence.

words.ex: The castle is a medieval building.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡是一座中世纪的建筑。
words.en: Relating to the Middle Ages, the period in European history from about the 5th century to the 15th century.

words.tr: phrase. 中世纪（约公元500年至1500年的欧洲历史时期）
words.ex: People lived in small villages during the middle ages.
words.ex_cn: 在中世纪，人们住在小村庄里。
words.en: The Middle Ages is the period in European history from the fall of the Roman Empire in the West (5th century) to the fall of Constantinople (15th century), or, more narrowly, from about 1000 to 1453.

words.ex: The colonisation of the land changed the lives of native people.
words.ex_cn: 这片土地的殖民化改变了原住民的生活。
words.en: Colonisation refers to the process by which a central system of power dominates the surrounding land and its components.

words.tr:
n. 风味；味道；
v. 给…添风味；
words.ex: This ice cream has a sweet flavour.
words.ex_cn: 这种冰淇淋有甜美的风味。
words.en: Flavour is the taste of a food or drink, especially when it is pleasant and distinctive.

words.ex: The ghost is invisible to the human eye.
words.ex_cn: 这个鬼魂肉眼看不见。
words.en: If something is invisible, you cannot see it because it is hidden or because it is very difficult to see.

words.ex: The water is toxic to fish.
words.ex_cn: 这种水对鱼是有毒的。
words.en: If a substance is toxic, it is poisonous.

words.ex: The frog is poisonous.
words.ex_cn: 这只青蛙是有毒的。
words.en: Something that is poisonous will kill you or make you ill if you eat it, drink it, or absorb it.

words.ex: The soldier wore camouflage to hide in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 士兵穿着伪装服在森林中隐藏自己。
